prompt: Where are the vertical asymptotes of $y = \tan x$?
hint: $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, and a fraction blows up when its DENOMINATOR is zero.

hints.text: $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, and a fraction blows up when its DENOMINATOR is zero.
So ask: for which $x$ is $\cos x = 0$?
Cosine is zero at $\frac{\pi}{2}$ and then every $\pi$ after that: $x = \frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi$.

explanation: The function is undefined exactly where $\cos x = 0$, which happens at $\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $-\frac{\pi}{2}$, and so on.
All of those are captured by $x = \frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi$, and the graph shoots off to infinity at each one.

alternativeExplanations.title: A vertical line has no slope
steps: $\tan x$ is the slope of the ray at angle $x$.
At $90^\circ$ that ray is straight up, and a vertical line has no slope at all.
That undefined slope is exactly the asymptote — and it repeats every half-turn.
